question: C-13 said separating direction-identity from dose needs a different design. Does pooling concept/codeword variants actually deliver one?
VERDICT: Pooling helps materially but does NOT dissolve the entanglement. d_surface's dose falls 0.840 -> 0.524 and the best ORTHOGONAL direction rises 0.114 -> 0.207 (1.8x), so a control can now carry real dose instead of scraps. But d_surface is still essentially PC1 (cos 0.9968), so the highest-dose direction remains d_surface-like and the top-dose region stays entangled.
actionable: A pooled multi-concept/multi-codeword bank is a genuinely better design for this question -- it is the cheapest available improvement and needs no new generations, only a refit over the existing three banks' cells. It is not sufficient on its own: dissolving the entanglement needs cells whose dominant variation is NOT the surface contrast.
